title: Joint X-ray
what: An X-ray of a joint. It shows the bones, the joint space, fractures, and signs of wear.
why: After an injury, for pain, swelling, clicking, or limited movement in a joint, or to check after treatment.
duration: usually 5 to 15 minutes in the room; the report the same or the next day
tell_doctor: If you are or might be pregnant
If the joint has a replacement, a plate, or screws
If it is hard to bend or straighten the joint

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: None needed. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Take off jewelry and anything metal in the area. Sometimes you are asked to change.

bring: Past X-rays of this joint, for comparison
steps: You uncover the joint and remove jewelry
The technician places the joint in the right position
Usually two images are taken from different sides
Sometimes both joints are imaged, or while standing under your weight
Each time, you keep still for a couple of seconds
feel: It does not hurt. The image takes a fraction of a second
Sometimes you need to hold an awkward position for a bit
With a fresh injury, positioning can hurt. Tell the technician
after: You can go about your day right away
Take the images and report to an orthopedic or trauma doctor

faq.q: Does an X-ray show ligaments and the meniscus?
faq.a: No, X-rays show bones. Ligaments and menisci are seen better on MRI or ultrasound.
Sometimes to compare it with the painful one. Your doctor decides.

reminders.text: Joint X-ray soon. Wear comfortable clothes and bring past X-rays.
